results.controlIntent: [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] are used to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
CM-3(1).r4 requires automated mechanisms to enforce change control — specifically that changes are documented, approved before deployment, and that unapproved changes are prohibited. Evidence from two sources reveals critical violations:

**Violation 1 — Hotfix bypassed approval gate entirely (UpdateEndpoint, 2026-03-15):**
CloudTrail event 3202b2ea shows that `data-scientist-jdoe` deployed a hotfix config (`churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`) to the endpoint on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z. The model registry (df0b7b54) contains only one entry (version 1, approved 2025-12-01), and no corresponding registry entry exists for this hotfix. This means the change was made without any documented approval in the registry — directly violating CM-3(1).r4(b), (d), and (e): no approval was sought, no approval was received, and the system did not prohibit the unapproved change.

**Violation 2 — Initial deployment sequencing anomaly (CreateEndpoint, 2025-12-01):**
CloudTrail event 3ff60d53 records the endpoint creation at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z. The registry approval timestamp is 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. While the raw timestamps suggest deployment occurred after approval, the CloudTrail note explicitly flags this as a change-control violation ("Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00"). This discrepancy — whether a timestamp error or a note reflecting a different reference point — itself indicates a documentation/audit integrity gap inconsistent with CM-3(1).r4(a) and (e).

**Summary:** At minimum, the March 2026 hotfix deployment with no registry entry is a clear, unambiguous violation of the requirement to prohibit changes until designated approvals are received. The automated change-control mechanism (model registry approval gate) was circumvented. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated notification mechanism (e.g., SNS, ticketing system) for approval requests or completion notifications — CM-3(1).r4(b) and (f) cannot be fully assessed.
No evidence of a time-bounded approval-pending alert mechanism — CM-3(1).r4(c) cannot be assessed.

The hotfix registry entry (if any exists outside SageMaker Model Registry) was not retrievable — a human attestation or additional tooling review would be needed to rule out an out-of-band approval process.
The conflicting timestamp note on the CreateEndpoint event requires human investigation to determine whether the initial deployment truly preceded approval or whether the note is erroneous.

payload.note: Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00 — change control not satisfied
